subject: Re: Project Nimbus kickoff: language-to-policy-code demo plan
body:
Hi both,

Status: the prompt library is in. LMPs now chain perception outputs into control primitives, and the hierarchical code-gen path (recursively generating helper functions) works — the model writes NumPy/Shapely code for the spatial-geometric cases like "move a bit to the left of the mug" unprompted.

Sim numbers: 46/50 tabletop pick-and-place instructions succeed, including held-out object names. Where it struggles: prescribing precise velocities from ambiguous language ("faster") is context-dependent, and on the real arm our impedance-controller primitive occasionally receives unsafe gain values.

Proposed mitigation: clamp gains in the API rather than trusting generated code, and keep a whitelist of importable libraries. Costs some generality, buys safety sign-off.

Risk to 4/27: real-platform integration is a week behind; Maren and I think it's recoverable.

Freya
